sentences: The seminar asks for stronger fixed-parameter inapproximability results that remain beyond known techniques even when Gap-ETH is assumed.
For k-Set Cover, one target is approximation hardness of order log^0.99(n), where n is the number of elements to cover.
A second target is to rule out every g(k)-factor FPT approximation for Exact k-Set Cover, whose promise is that a size-k cover consisting of disjoint sets exists.
It also asks for o(k)-factor hardness of Densest k-Subgraph with perfect completeness under Gap-ETH, matching a result based on the Strongish Planted Clique Hypothesis.
In particular, hardness with disjoint-cover completeness would support further reductions to coding and lattice problems.

sentences: Given a graph with m edges, the source asks whether deleting at most m/6 vertices always suffices to make the remaining graph planar.
Deleting a vertex also removes every edge incident to it, so one deletion can eliminate several overlapping obstructions to planarity.
The statement is an extremal existence claim over all graphs, with the allowed deletion budget determined by the edge count.
A counterexample would require more than m/6 vertex deletions for every way of obtaining a planar graph.
Resolving the question would quantify how much vertex removal is guaranteed to repair nonplanarity using only the number of edges.
correction_reason: The previous summary described a parameterized algorithmic research direction; the saved question instead states a specific universal m/6 planarization bound.

sentences: The k-Disjoint Paths problem asks for mutually vertex-disjoint paths connecting k prescribed pairs of terminals.
The selected question asks whether positive instances on n-vertex graphs have polynomial-time-verifiable certificates whose size is polynomial in k plus log n.
Such a bound would shorten the evidence needed to certify a solution, since explicitly listing all the paths can require much longer witnesses.
The source notes that the planar version already admits certificates of size polynomial in k.
It separately asks for certificates of size polynomial in k plus log n on acyclic digraphs, where the dependence on log n matters because parameterization by k is W[1]-hard.
correction_reason: The previous summary assigned the selected question to Subset Sum from the paper title; the actual concluding paragraph concerns short certificates for k-Disjoint Paths.

sentences: Matroid Median selects a feasible set of facilities from a matroid and minimizes the sum of distances from clients to their closest selected facilities.
The cited paper gives a (2+ε)-approximation algorithm with fixed-parameter running time.
Because k-Median is a special case, Matroid Median also inherits the paper's Gap-ETH-based hardness for approximation within 1+2/e−ε.
The open question is to close the gap between this inherited lower bound and the (2+ε) algorithm.
A tight result would reveal how much additional approximation difficulty comes from matroid constraints when parameterized computation is allowed.
correction_reason: The previous summary left the variant unresolved and centered k-Median and k-Means; the remaining gap after Theorem 3 specifically concerns Matroid Median.

sentences: Approximating treewidth means constructing a tree decomposition whose width is controlled in relation to the smallest possible width.
The cited paper already gives a 2^O(k)n-time algorithm that returns a decomposition of width at most 2k+1 or determines that the graph has treewidth greater than k.
Its concluding question asks for a constant-factor approximation in c^k n time with a small exponential base c.
The goal is to reduce that base while preserving linear dependence on graph size and a constant approximation guarantee.
This could make decomposition construction more practical for the many graph algorithms that use treewidth as a parameter.
